title: Why Magical Realism Still Holds a Mirror to Our World
excerpt: From García Márquez to Salman Rushdie, magical realism has always been more than a literary device — it is an act of resistance, a way of seeing the world beneath the world. In an age of relentless rationalism, its relevance has never felt more urgent.
author: Ayesha Siddiqui

title: The Lost Art of Letter Writing
excerpt: Before the tyranny of instant messaging, letters breathed. They aged. They smelled of the sender's home. We explore what we lost when we traded pen for pixel.
author: Maryam Farooq

title: Spoken Word Is Literature Too
excerpt: The page and the stage have always been at odds, but they needn't be. We argue that spoken word poetry deserves a seat at the literary canon's table.
author: Zain ul Abideen

title: Reading Urdu Literature Through an English Lens
excerpt: What happens when you apply Western critical theory to the ghazals of Ghalib or the prose of Manto? The results are illuminating — and sometimes unsettling.
author: Laila Zafar

title: Fan Fiction and the Future of Storytelling
excerpt: Once dismissed as frivolous imitation, fan fiction has become a training ground for some of today's most creative storytellers. This is its literary defence.
author: Sana Tariq

title: On Grief, Silence, and the Poems We Never Finish
excerpt: Some poems live only in drafts. They are not failed works — they are the rawest, most honest things a writer will ever produce. A meditation on incompletion.
author: Hira Anwar

title: The Comma and the Breath: Punctuation as Emotion
excerpt: Emily Dickinson's dashes, Cormac McCarthy's refusal of apostrophes — punctuation has always been a vehicle for feeling. A close reading of marks that matter.
author: Hassan Raza
